commit.message:
test: do not assert a HEAD response body through inject() (#7148)

Two tests read the body of a HEAD response through `fastify.inject()`:

- "Should allow registering a constrained GET route after a constrained
HEAD route" (`test/constrained-routes.test.js`) checks `res.payload ===
'custom HEAD response'`;
- "fastify.all should add all the methods to the same url"
(`test/internals/all.test.js`) parses the HEAD payload as JSON.

A real server sends no body for HEAD, and fastify/light-my-request#408
makes `inject()` do the same. @gurgunday approved the behaviour there
but asked for fastify core to be updated before it ships, since these
two tests would fail with it.

These tests now check the response headers instead of the body:

- The constrained route test asserts the `content-type` set by the
custom HEAD handler (`text/plain`) and the `content-length` of `'custom
HEAD response'`. That still shows the custom handler ran, not a HEAD
route derived from the GET one.
- The `fastify.all` test asserts the HEAD response's `content-length`
matches `JSON.stringify({ method: 'HEAD' })` and parses the body only
for the other methods.

Both files pass with the current light-my-request release and with the
#408 branch symlinked into `node_modules` (26 tests each time), so this
can land before or after it. ESLint is clean on both files.

(cherry picked from commit 78d68b2225baa3b7e05ebb5522239f40a4bcf6e8)
